answer: Proof-of-Agent beats Sybil by pricing identities in graded judgment, not keys. A clone swarm minted at dawn gains nothing: every umber-dull copy still owes a fresh, peer-attested answer under slashing. Faking one head is cheap; faking a thousand means producing a thousand distinct, defensible chains of reasoning that graders actually pass. No oasis of free throughput exists, so attacker cost scales linearly with heads while reward stays gated on quality.
